skill.name: coding-html
skill.description: When html or jinja are being written or edited.
skill.body:
# HTML coding standards

## Syntax & Style
Spacing: Keep vertical spacing compact (no excessive blank lines).
Readability: Prioritize readable code over "clever" one-liners.

## CSS
**In-line css**: Prefer use of classes from .css files to in-line css, unless explicitely justified.

## JS
**In-line js**: Prefer including from functions in .js files to in-line js, unless explicitly justified.

## Comments
**Preserve comments**: Do NOT delete existing, still relevant comments.

## Logic & Operations
**File Collisions**: If a file exists, append _[timestamp] to the new filename.
**Simplicity**: Choose the simplest working solution.

generated_query: I'm updating my company's website and need to add a new pricing page. I have an existing Django project with a `base.html` template, a `style.css` containing classes like `.pricing-card`, `.feature-list`, and `.toggle-btn`, and a `script.js` that already has a `togglePlan()` function. I need you to create a new Jinja template called `pricing.html` that inherits from `base.html`. The template should display three pricing plans (Basic, Pro, Enterprise) using CSS classes from `style.css` (no inline styles) and include a monthly/yearly toggle that calls the existing JavaScript function from `script.js` (no inline scripts). Also, if a file named `pricing.html` already exists in my templates folder, append the current timestamp to the new filename (e.g., `pricing_202310051430.html`). Keep the code clean and readable, with minimal blank lines, and preserve any existing comments in the files you reference.

edit_instructions.target_text: **File Collisions**: If a file exists, append _[timestamp] to the new filename.
edit_instructions.rationale: Without the file collision rule, the skill would overwrite an existing pricing.html, failing the user's requirement to append timestamp.
